aboutPage.heading: About Troop 65
aboutPage.intro: Troop 65 is a Scouts BSA troop in Long Beach, California. We have been meeting since 1937. We are part of the Iron Star District of the Long Beach Area Council.

heroImage.alt: Troop 65 scouts in purple shirts under the entrance gate at the 2026 Firestone camporee

sections.heading: Since 1937
sections.text:
The troop started in 1937. Our motto is on the logo: Serving God and Country since 1937.

In 1997 the troop turned 60. A painted mural from that year is still on the wall of our meeting room.

People know us as the Purple Plague. You will see a lot of purple shirts at our meetings and campouts.

[NEEDS INFO] More of the troop's history. Who started it, where it first met, and anything the old-timers like to tell.

images.alt: Painted Troop 65 60th anniversary mural with mountains and the years 1937 to 1997

sections.heading: The Eagle Lair
sections.text:
When a scout earns Eagle with Troop 65, their name is burned into a piece of leather and hung in our Eagle Lair. The troop has kept this tradition for more than 70 years, and there are now more than 200 names on the wall.

Come to a meeting and you can read every one.

sections.heading: Four patrols
sections.text:
Every scout belongs to a patrol. A patrol is a small group that meets together, camps together, and has its own patrol leader. We have four.

The Eagles are our longest running patrol. They are known for showing up to troop events.

The Sabertooths are our newest patrol. They have been around for 15 years.

The Diamondbacks are built on the Scout Oath and Scout Law, and they want to keep growing.

The Falcons are a hard-working patrol that welcomes new scouts on every outing.

sections.heading: Scouts run the meetings
sections.text:
Scouts hold 17 troop jobs. The Senior Patrol Leader runs the troop with help from the Assistant Senior Patrol Leader and the four patrol leaders. Other scouts serve as Quartermaster, Scribe, Historian, Librarian, Chaplain Aide, Bugler, Webmaster, Outdoor Ethics Guide, Recruitment Advisor, and Troop Instructor.

The Patrol Leaders Council meets on the 4th Tuesday of each month to plan what the troop does next.

images.alt: A scout in uniform in front of the American flag and troop banners in the meeting room

sections.heading: Adults help
sections.text: Adult leaders and a troop committee of parents support the scouts. There is a Scoutmaster, assistant Scoutmasters for each patrol, and committee members who handle jobs like advancement, equipment, and fundraising.

sections.heading: Campouts
sections.text:
Campouts are optional. Most run Friday night to Sunday morning.

In 2026 the troop went to Winter Camp at Camp Emerson, held a lock-in overnight at the church, went to Desert Camp in the Mecca Wilderness, and spent a weekend at pre-summer camp in Chino Hills.

sections.heading: Pre-summer camp at Chino Hills State Park, 2026
sections.text: The campground had lots of open space, so most of the scouts played Three-Flags-Up and baseball. We also went on a hike, which was good practice for the longer hikes coming up.

sections.heading: Firestone Camporee, 2026
sections.text: Troop 65 competed at the council camporee at Firestone Scout Reservation. We did not win as many trophies this year, but we had a great time. It was the first taste of T65 competition for our new scouts.

sections.heading: Service
sections.text:
We help at Lakewood Village Community Church, where we meet. In 2026 that meant Scout Sunday, Palm Sunday, Good Friday, and Easter Sunday. Scouts also put out flags for Memorial Day.

Scouts working on Eagle plan and lead a service project, and the troop comes out to help.

The troop raises money with a pancake breakfast.

sections.heading: Advancement
sections.text:
Scouts work through the ranks from Scout to Eagle and earn merit badges along the way. Scouts and parents can track progress in the Scoutbook app.

After a Scoutmaster Conference, a scout signs up for a Board of Review. Boards of Review are held on the 4th Tuesday of each month.

At Courts of Honor, scouts receive their new ranks and merit badges.

sections.heading: Leadership training
sections.text: Scouts who hold troop jobs can take National Youth Leadership Training (NYLT). Five scouts from Troop 65 have finished it.

joinPage.heading: Visit a meeting
joinPage.intro: The best way to see if Troop 65 is a fit is to come to a Tuesday meeting. Fill out the form and we will look for you.

heroImage.alt: Scouts at a camp table with a stove and gear, patrol flag behind them

steps.heading: Fill out the form
steps.text: Tell us who is coming and which Tuesday.

steps.heading: Come at 6:30
steps.text: Meetings are at Lakewood Village Community Church, 4515 Sunfield Ave. The troop meets in the church basement.

steps.heading: Watch a meeting
steps.text: Patrols meet first. At 7:30 the whole troop meets together. We finish at 8:30 pm.
